Title/Hook: 6 months ago, I couldn't write a single line of code.
Body:
Today, I've built 26 working software tools.

The difference wasn't learning to code. It was learning to collaborate with AI.

Here's what nobody tells non-technical founders:

You don't need to become a developer.
You need to become a great communicator.

I'm not writing Python or JavaScript. I'm writing clear instructions.

My process:
1. I describe what I want in plain English
2. Claude Code builds it
3. I test it (does it do what I asked?)
4. I share the error if it breaks
5. We iterate until it works

The tools I've built in the last 6 months:

- A Personal Operating System that prioritizes my projects automatically
- Job listing scrapers that categorize 50K+ listings with AI
- Content systems that turn project updates into posts
- Vendor quote automation that finds contacts in 5 minutes vs 2 hours
- Financial analysis dashboards (analyzed 6 years of nonprofit data in one afternoon)

My competitive advantage isn't technical skill.

It's knowing exactly what I need and being able to articulate it clearly.

Takeaway: The best 'code' I write is plain English. If you can explain a problem clearly to a human, you can explain it to AI.

Title/Hook: How I generate a week of social content in 10 minutes
Body:
I used to spend 10+ hours every week brainstorming content.

Now my AI system does it in minutes.

The secret: I stopped asking AI to 'be creative.'

Instead, I feed it proven frameworks.

Here's the exact system:

1. Capture my actual work
Every project update, lesson learned, and breakthrough gets logged automatically.

2. Match to viral patterns
My system knows 97+ hook formulas:
- Contrarian: 'Why X is actually wrong'
- Transformation: 'Before vs After'
- How-to: 'The exact process for X'

3. Generate variations
One project update becomes 5+ content pieces.

4. Apply my voice
I documented my writing patterns specifically.

Results after 30 days:
- 47 hooks generated
- 10 hrs/week saved
- Higher engagement

Takeaway: Content frameworks are just structured prompts. Feed AI the framework. Let it apply your context.

Title/Hook: Why your AI prompts are failing (and it's not what you think)
Body:
Most people write prompts like 'Write me a viral tweet.'

Then they're disappointed when AI outputs generic garbage.

AI doesn't need creativity. It needs frameworks.

Bad prompt: 'Help me brainstorm content ideas.'

Good prompt: 'Apply the Contrarian Hook formula to my project update. The formula: Challenge common assumption + reveal better approach. My update: I built a job scraper that processes 1000 listings in seconds.'

How to do this yourself:
1. Find 10 posts in your niche that performed well
2. Identify the structure
3. Turn that structure into a template
4. Ask AI to apply that template to YOUR content

Takeaway: The frameworks do the creative heavy lifting. Build a library of frameworks you can combine and reuse.
CTA: What framework would you want to template first?

Title/Hook: The exact process I use to build tools with Claude Code (as a non-developer)
Body:
People ask how I build software without a technical background.

Here's my exact process:

Step 1: Define the Problem Clearly
Not 'I want a scraper.' Instead: specific inputs, outputs, and constraints.

Step 2: Start with the Simplest Version
Always ask: 'What's the minimal version that would be useful?'

Step 3: Describe, Don't Dictate
Describe WHAT you need, not HOW to build it. Let Claude choose.

Step 4: Test Immediately
Run the code right away. Errors are feedback, not failure.

Step 5: Document What Works
Every successful pattern goes into my CLAUDE.md file.

Takeaway: You're not a coder. You're a product manager with an infinitely patient engineering team.
